Chapter 8: Designing a Life of Ongoing Experimentation.
So, now that you’ve built a foundation of financial and relational freedom, what’s next? Well, the real magic starts when you begin seeing your life as a series of ongoing experiments.
Instead of searching for that one perfect solution or waiting for everything to line up just right, imagine shifting your focus to continuous learning, adapting, and growing along the way.
This mindset is all about curiosity and humility. Let’s be real—no plan ever survives reality untouched, does it? The truth is, the best way to figure out what works is simply to try, pay attention, and adjust as you go. Life gets a lot more fun—and a lot less stressful—when it’s about exploration rather than rigid, unbending goals.
Here’s a simple framework to keep your experiments moving forward:
First, set small, testable goals. You don’t need to overhaul your life overnight. Try out new habits or routines on a small scale—just enough to see what happens.
Next, track your results. Notice what feels energizing or meaningful, and be honest about what drains or frustrates you.
Then, adjust and iterate. Use what you learn to tweak your approach. Let go of what doesn’t work, and double down on the things that do.
Finally, embrace failure as feedback. Setbacks aren’t proof that you’re not good enough—they’re just information to help you course-correct.
For example, if you’re thinking about a career change, you might start by taking a class, volunteering, or picking up a freelance project in that new field—just to test the waters before making a big leap. Or, if you want to get healthier, you could try out different workouts or eating habits and see what actually fits your body and your lifestyle.
The best part? This approach takes the pressure off. You don’t have to “get it right” the first time. Instead, you build up flexibility and resilience, making it so much easier to adapt when life throws you a curveball.
Over time, these little experiments help you learn more about yourself—and boost your confidence, too.
Designing your life as an experiment also means staying open to surprise and delight. Some of the most rewarding moments come from trying something new, even when you have no idea how it’ll turn out. By staying curious and willing to learn, you keep life fresh and exciting.
So, here’s the key takeaway: ongoing experimentation is a powerful antidote to perfectionism and rigidity. It turns your journey toward freedom into a process of discovery—where each step brings you new insights and unexpected opportunities.
